_comment: Project state for the JVTO content ecosystem. Read at session start by jvto-ops (scripts/session-brief.mjs) and by checkers that would otherwise freeze a policy constant in their own source. Shape is documented in the plugin at docs/goals-schema.md. Edit this file; do not duplicate its facts into a checker.

baseline.note: Measured against the live site over all 291 sitemap routes. The auditor does not strip <header> (on most routes here that element is the page hero) and does not treat low fact density on crew pages as a defect (those pages are built from verbatim guest reviews).

decisions.why: robots.ts already allowed every AI-training crawler and AEO/GEO visibility is a stated goal of this site; the header said ai-train=no and contradicted it.
decisions.note: jvto-web/scripts/audit-generative-visibility.mjs froze ai-train=no in its own source and reported eleven false failures for eight days. It now reads policies.contentSignal from this file. A checker that freezes a policy is a checker that will contradict its owner.

decisions.decision: check-answer-first reports the three-fact rule as a warning, not an error. Word count (40-60) and volatile numbers written as literals stay errors.
decisions.why: The rule fires on 25 of 56 live blocks. It runs from a per-edit hook, and a checker that fires on 40% of a corpus gets muted. Word count and literals are objective; the fact list is a heuristic that was widened twice during the plugin build.
decisions.openQuestion: Resolved in practice: all 56 blocks now pass. The rule stayed a warning, but the 22 it flagged were fixed rather than tolerated — and 13 of the 25 original findings turned out to be the checker undercounting categories the spec names (recurring periods, attributed person names, and any number with a unit rather than a unit from a hardcoded list of six).

decisions.why: Its skills document internal deploy protocols, infrastructure paths and incident history. Publishing is a separate, reversible owner decision.

The repo carried 200 in display_height_m and the summary against '~100 m' in hero_meta_override and hub_elevation_label, plus two duplicates in jvto-web fallbacks. 200 m agrees with independent tourism references that also rank it the tallest waterfall on Java, which the site's own chips already claimed. The ~620-1000 m figures in circulation are the site's elevation above sea level, not the drop — altitude 620 keeps that separate.
decisions.note: Recorded here rather than in the destination content file: an internal maintenance note placed there was serialized into the page payload and shipped to the browser.

decisions.decision: The canonical and duplicate-intent checks in `npm run validate routes` are retired, not restored.
decisions.why: src/lib/registry/pages.ts was deleted on 2026-08-15 in 3925805f and nothing under src/ has imported it since. The redirect-vs-filesystem reconciliation, which never needed the registry, stays: 207 redirect and gone sources against 41 static routes, verified against a deliberately broken redirect.

decisions.decision: A review may be attributed to a product by reading the review text, but only when exactly one product fits, and the record must say so via packageAttribution.
decisions.why: Twelve products showed no reviews while 71 reviews sat unattributed, and many of those name their itinerary outright. Matching against each product's itinerary, name and paid add-ons placed 19 of them and filled five empty products. The provenance field exists so a later reader can tell a deduction from an observation — a review states which tour someone took, and a derived slug is our reading of it, not their statement.
decisions.note: Order of mention was rejected as evidence. Two Surabaya 3D2N products differ in nothing but the order their names list the same three destinations, and guests list by impression. Five reviews that only order could separate were left unattributed rather than assigned on that basis.

backlog.title: BBKSDA circular SE.35/K2/BIDTEK.1/KSA/1/2024 is cited but not held
backlog.evidence: credentials.json carries it with evidenceStatus media_sourced and no documentUrl or sha256. If the copy found is a scan, publish it as-is and hash that file rather than retyping it. If its number or date differs from what is cited in 12+ places, raise it before publishing.

backlog.title: Seven tour packages have no attributed reviews
backlog.status: open — data, not code; the inferable share has been worked
backlog.evidence: 169 of 221 reviews now carry a packageSlug, covering ten of seventeen products. 19 of those were derived from the review text on 2026-08-26 and carry a packageAttribution object recording the method, the confidence and the evidence; the rest came with the booking. Rules and rejected cases are in docs/review-package-attribution.md. The remaining 52 unattributed reviews cannot be placed: 47 name no destination at all, and 5 name a combination more than one product covers. Closing the last seven means capturing the package at review time.
